subject: RFP: Support & Customer Success Questionnaire - TAM coverage and escalation paths
messages:
From: Matt Briggs <matt.briggs@acmehealth.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP: Support & CS Questionnaire - TAM coverage, escalation paths

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking this RFP. We're consolidating vendor responses and need a completed vendor-side questionnaire focused on Support and Customer Success. The specific items we are prioritizing: TAM coverage model (ratios, assigned hours, named vs pooled TAMs), escalation path and contact matrix for P1/P2 incidents, support hours and SLA targets for incident acknowledgement/response/resolution, and a sample incident communication template.

Can you provide a completed RFP spreadsheet (we attached Acme_RFP_Support_Questionnaire.xlsx) and any supporting docs that outline on-call coverage and escalation procedures? Also please call out the differences between hosted (Redwood API) and private deployments where applicable.

We are on a compressed schedule — would appreciate the response by Friday 20 Mar. If you can, include an escalation matrix with primary/secondary contacts and target response SLAs.

Best,
Matt
Matt Briggs
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Health
Attachments: Acme_RFP_Support_Questionnaire.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Matt Briggs <matt.briggs@acmehealth.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP: Support & CS Questionnaire - TAM coverage, escalation paths

Hi Matt —

Thanks for sharing the questionnaire and the timeline. Please find attached a first-pass response packet (Redwood_RFP_Support_Response_20260318.pdf) and our Support Blueprint that details our TAM model and incident comms. High-level answers inline below; full details are in the attached PDF and the shared Drive doc.

- TAM coverage: For enterprise customers we assign a named Technical Account Manager (TAM) after contract signature. Typical onboarding ratio is 1 TAM : 20 active instances/users; for strategic accounts (annual recurring revenue > $1M) we offer 1 : 8. TAMs cover operational guidance, playbook reviews, and monthly business reviews. On-call support for P1s is provided 24x7 via our escalation engineer pool; TAMs are informed and coordinate post-incident reviews.

- Support hours & SLAs: Standard support hours: 9am–6pm local business days (regional) with 24x7 coverage for P1 incidents for all enterprise tiers. SLA targets (acknowledge/initial response): P1: 15 min, P2: 2 hours, P3: 8 business hours. Resolution targets depend on severity and agreed runbooks; see attached matrix.

- Escalation path: Primary (Support Ops) -> Secondary (Triage Engineers) -> TAM -> On-call Senior Engineer -> Escalation to Platform Reliability Lead. We include named contacts in our escalation matrix once account setup is complete.

- Incident comms: We provide incident-descriptor templates, cadence (initial acknowledgement, 1-hour status updates for P1 until resolution, post-incident summary within 48 hours), and access to a shared incident channel (Slack/Teams) if requested.

I'll schedule a 30-minute call with Rishi (sales lead) and Tessa (Customer Success) to walk through any items you want clarified. Are you available Monday 22 Mar 10:30–11:00 PT?

Links/attachments: Redwood_Support_Blueprint.pdf, Redwood_RFP_Support_Response_20260318.pdf, shared Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleLink

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_RFP_Support_Response_20260318.pdf (pdf), Redwood_Support_Blueprint.pdf (pdf)
From: Matt Briggs <matt.briggs@acmehealth.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP: Support & CS Questionnaire - TAM coverage, escalation paths

Marissa,

Thanks for the quick turnaround — that helps. A couple of clarifying questions from our infra team before we finalize: 

1) Can you confirm whether the named TAM is part of the 24x7 escalation chain (i.e., are they paged for P1s), or are TAMs purely post-incident coordinators?
2) For on-call escalation, what is your target time from detection to engineering page for P1s? You mention an initial response SLA of 15 minutes — is that from detection or from ticket creation?
3) We would like a simple escalation matrix that shows role, contact method (pager/email/phone), and SLA for each step — could you provide that as a spreadsheet?

Also, to move procurement forward we'll need suggested contract language for incident communications (acknowledgement cadence, interim updates, post-incident report timing) so our legal team can insert it into the SOW.

If you can get those items by EOD Friday that should keep us on schedule.

Regards,
Matt
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: FW: RFP: Support & CS Questionnaire - action items and draft language (internal)

Team —

Looping you in to finalize the items Acme asked for. Key asks: named TAM role in escalation path, precise timing language for detection vs ticket creation, and a one-sheet escalation matrix (role, contact method, SLA). Procurement also wants suggested contract/SOW language for incident communications.

Proposed answers (please review and edit directly in the attached matrix):
- TAM involvement: Named TAM is not the primary 24x7 pager for P1 triage (that is handled by our on-call engineering rota). TAMs are always included in the P1 notification stream and own the customer communications and RCA coordination post-remediation. Wording suggestion: "Redwood will assign a named Technical Account Manager to Acme after contract signature. The TAM will be notified of all P1 incidents and will coordinate customer-facing communications and post-incident reviews; primary real-time triage will be handled by Redwood's on-call engineering team."

- Detection vs ticket: Our monitoring systems page on-call engineers automatically on detection. SLA deadlines (acknowledgement/initial response) are calculated from ticket creation time in our support system. Proposed wording: "Response SLAs are measured from ticket creation in Redwood's support portal. Monitoring systems will page on-call engineering upon detection; tickets are generated automatically for tracking and SLA measurement."

- Escalation matrix: see attached Proposed_Escalation_Matrix.xlsx (we should include phone/pager/email columns and escalation windows).

Vivek — can you confirm whether the communication cadence needs any additional compliance wording for Acme's regulated data workflows? Tessa / Rishi — please proof the proposed contract language for the SOW and signoff. I'll send a customer-facing update once we have your changes.

Thanks,
Marissa
Attachments: Proposed_Escalation_Matrix.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Matt Briggs <matt.briggs@acmehealth.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP: Support & CS Questionnaire - TAM coverage and escalation paths

Hi Matt —

Appreciate the follow-up. Attached is an updated single-sheet response and the escalation matrix: Redwood_RFP_Support_Response_Updated.pdf and Proposed_Escalation_Matrix.xlsx. To confirm the items you called out: 

- TAM participation: TAMs are informed and alerted for P1s but are not the primary paged responder. They own customer communications and the post-incident RCA.
- Detection vs ticket: Our monitoring pages on-call immediately on detection. SLAs in the RFP are measured from ticket creation in our support portal; tickets are automatically created at detection.
- Escalation matrix: included — shows role, contact method (phone/pager/email), and SLA window for each step.

Below is suggested SOW language for incident communications your legal team can use or adapt:

"Incident Communications: Redwood will acknowledge P1 incidents within fifteen (15) minutes of ticket creation and provide hourly status updates until remediation is achieved. An initial incident summary will be provided within one (1) hour of ticket creation when feasible. A post-incident report (root cause analysis and mitigation actions) will be delivered within forty-eight (48) hours following incident resolution. Parties may agree to alternate timelines in a mutually executed SOW."

Next steps: can we confirm a 30-minute call on Monday 22 Mar at 10:30 PT to answer any follow-ups? I can share a draft SOW clause in DocuSign for easier redlining if that helps: https://www.docusign.com/initiator/abc123

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_RFP_Support_Response_Updated.pdf (pdf), Proposed_Escalation_Matrix.xlsx (xlsx)
